newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BNDES sees Brazil's 1997 trade gap at over $8 bln.
newsitem.headline: BNDES sees Brazil's 1997 trade gap at over $8 bln.

text.p: Brazil is likely to post a trade deficit of between $8 billion and $9 billion in 1997, the country's National Development Bank (BNDES) said in a report.
BNDES said Brazilian imports are expected to keep growing faster than exports, reaching over $58 billion, while exports are likely to increase to $49 billion.
Last year Brazil posted a record trade deficit of $5.576 billion, with exports of $47.747 billion and imports of $53.286 billion.

The higher projected trade gap is not worrisome as it is compatible with the country's capacity of financing its current account deficit, said Fabio Giambiagi, an economist at BNDES, which is the main provider of credit lines for exporters.

Giambiagi also said the bank's estimates consider the positive effects of the elimination of the ICMS tax on exports of primary and semi-manufactured goods. It does not take into account other export-boosting measures, introduced late last year, which he expects will have a positive impact only in the second half of 1997.
